trial_court: District Munsif's Court, Gingee, O.S. No. 595 of 1989
case_name: Gopala Gounder vs Kasi Ammal And Anr.

parties.respondent_defendant: First plaintiff (wife) and second plaintiff (minor son)

facts_of_case: The defendant's wife and minor son claimed maintenance under Section 18 of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act. The trial court held that both plaintiffs are entitled to maintenance and awarded Rs. 300 and Rs. 400 as maintenance respectively. The defendant appealed against this decision.

legal_principles.principle: Concurrent findings of fact cannot be upset by minor inconsistencies.
legal_principles.held: The inconsistencies, even if there is any, are only minor, and they cannot upset the concurrent findings of fact.
cited_cases: Gopala Gounder vs Kasi Ammal And Anr. on 2 November, 1998

legal_principles.principle: An illegitimate son or daughter is also a dependant entitled to maintenance.
legal_principles.held: Section 21 of that Act defines as to who are the dependants entitled to maintenance. An illegitimate son or daughter is also a dependant under Section 21.

legal_principles.principle: A child born of a null and void marriage shall be deemed to be legitimate for the purpose of maintenance.
legal_principles.held: Notwithstanding the fact that a marriage which is null and void under Section 11 of the Hindu Marriage Act, a child born of such marriage shall be deemed to be legitimate for the said purpose.

outcome.final_order: The lower appellate court affirmed the finding of a valid marriage between the parties, but declared it null and void since the first marriage was subsisting. Arrears of maintenance were also awarded.
